 Placer County, Still Murderous After All These Years. Kubbys Find Secret Death Warrant Signed by Disqualified Judge. Key To Canadian Refuge, If Not Justice In California.

VANCOUVER -- American medical marijuana refugee Steve Kubby and his  family have been ordered to leave Canada on January 12th or face  arrest and forcible removal to the US. Their last-ditch appeal will  be heard on January 9, 2006.

Michele Kubby warns that if they are not granted an emergency stay,  Steve Kubby will be handed over to US authorities under a no-bail  warrant to be sent to California, where he faces jail for possession  of minute quantities of mescaline and psilocin, which the police  extracted from remnants of a cactus and a mushroom found in a guest  bedroom in the Kubbys California home.

On November 22, the Canadian Border Services Agency rejected the  Kubbys last request for protection in what is called a Pre-Removal  Risk Assessment (PRRA), saying, It has been determined that you  would not be subject to  risk to life if returned to your country

The PRRA officer refused to consider a letter from Dr. Joseph Connors  of the BC Cancer Agency, who was chosen by Immigration Canada. Dr.  Connors did confirm that Mr. Kubby does indeed have a rare form of  cancer which is controlled only by marijuana, but only new evidence  is permitted under the PRRA rules, as determined by CBSA.  Consequently, the Pre-Removal Risk Assessment could then say that  there is no evidence of risk to Mr. Kubbys life, even though the  provinces leading oncologist says otherwise, and the PRRA officer  noted Dr. Connors letter.
See
 A Critique of the Kubby Refugee Ruling: What Is It About Dead That You Dont Understand?

In addition, the officer declined to consider two sworn affidavits by  prominent Seattle attorneys that Steven Tuck, another American  medical marijuana refugee, did not receive even basic medical care  while in US custody. Tuck was taken in handcuffs from a gurney in the  ER of a Vancouver hospital on October 7th and turned over to the US  authorities. CBSA officers told Tucks friends that he was being  taken to a hospital in the US. Instead, he was simply jailed.
See
Steve Tuck Is A Free Man. Vindicated. Recuperating from Five Year Ordeal. Will Return to Mining Business in Canada After First Of Year.

The PRRA official said, I do not give this information considerable  weight, as I find that the information comes not from disinterested  sources, but from this individuals counsel. I am unable to find any trustworthy and independent sources to corroborate that the  individual concerned was not given proper medical attention while  jailed.

One of the attorneys, Hunter MacDonald, only represented Tuck at one  hearing as a courtesy to the attorney Douglas Hiatt, who was  representing Tuck pro bono. Neither have been paid by Tuck.  

Michele Kubby noted, In the US, attorneys are officers of the court  and swearing to false affidavits  especially those questioning the  administration of justice  could result in serious legal sanctions.  The idea that these two men are not trustworthy is absurd. They just don't want to admit that they almost killed Tuck.

Moreover, there is no evidence that the PRRA official ever attempted  to get any confirmation of Tucks treatment. (Tuck was treated at a Seattle hospital after his release from custody and given  prescriptions for antibiotics and pain medications that he was never  given in two American jails.)
(MarijuanaNews note: Needless to say, I am particularly outraged by this attempt to avoid responsibility for the consequences of the CBSAs abuse of Steve Tuck, who suffered terribly for a week and has still not recovered fully. As noted, there is no evidence that the CBSA official made any effort to find out what really happened to Tuck. They never asked the Kubbys or the lawyers for any contact information. These little apparatchiks can lie and send people to their deaths and not be held responsible.)

Michele Kubby said, On the basis of this obvious bias, we will be  arguing that institutional PRRA is prejudiced and lacks institutional  independence and impartiality, and a stay of the departure must be  granted while the Courts examine the legal basis of the entire system.

Mrs. Kubby said, I really fear for my husbands life. He could not  survive the abuse that nearly killed Steve Tuck, and, as Dr. Conners  confirmed, he must have cannabis to live.

Despite the threat to his life, Steve Kubby remains both defiant and  optimistic. When the CBSA official told them that their PRRA had been  rejected, Kubby told the CBSA official that he was relieved, because  if the PRRA had been accepted the Kubbys would not have been able to  challenge the law itself.

Kubby says, We told them that they lacked both the knowledge to  reach a proper decision and the legal authority to act. Clearly, they  dont know the law. They could not even cite the statutory basis of  their power. In fact, the CBSA is a part of the Justice Department,  not Immigration, which is supposed to handle these matters. We are putting the government on trial.

"The stakes are very high for me and my family, but they are also  very high for the people of Canada. Are they ruled by just laws, or by arbitrary bureaucracy that claims the power of life and death, but  hides from responsibility for the consequences of their actions, as  they did with Steve Tuck?
(MarijuanaNews note: Now is the time for Kubby's supporters -- and friends of freedom everywhere -- to rally behind them.)
